chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ja'far, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Abu Ja'far! What do you say about chess (al-shatranj) with which people play?' He said, 'My father Ali ibn al-Husayn informed me from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever speaks, and his speech is for other than the remembrance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is vain; and whoever is silent, and his silence is for other than the remembrance of Allah, is heedless.' Then he was silent, so the man stood up and departed.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on chess in Shia Islam based on the hadith of Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the Imams from the Prophet, establishes the ethical basis for the ruling on chess by framing it as a distraction from dhikr. It highlights the concept of 'ghaflah' (heedlessness), where speech or silence not dedicated to God becomes vain, thereby providing a theological foundation for its prohibition in Shia jurisprudence.
